title.narrative: Output 1.4. Increased capacity of Member States to improve social dialogue and labour relations laws, processes and institutions

description.narrative:
Between October 2022 and May 2023, social dialogue and dispute prevention and resolution institutions from Zanzibar; [Labour Advisory Board (LAB) and Dispute Handling Unit] were reformed and capacitated to execute their mandates and responsibilities, to better respond to emerging challenges in the world of work. As for the DHU the intervention focused on strengthening the capacities of arbitrators on arbitration skills and writing of awards to effectively execute their mandate; and on building the capacity of the Tripartite Committee on Dispute Resolution on playing its oversight role on the performance of the DHU.
As for the LAB, it involved capacity building in the application of the SAM-SDI method to assess the effectiveness and inclusivity of the institution in the execution of its mandate Between July 2022 and May 2023, utilizing resources available under the UNDP Multi Partner Trust Fund Office (One fund), UNDP funded Improved labour market governance and promotion of tripartism TZA/18/02/OUF and Enhancing implementation of labour standards by ending violence against women and children through a social dialogue framework; TZA/20/01/OUF, the ILO implemented training activities to build social dialogue capacities of all members and the secretariat of the LAB. With the enhanced capacity on social dialogue and tripartism, labour relations have improved among the constituents in Zanzibar. In addition, capacity was built for members of the LAB and secretariat on the application of the ILO SAM-SDI to assess the effectiveness and inclusivity of the institution. An action plan for reform has been adopted. Further under the same one fund framework, the ILO took measures to strengthen technical capacities of all DHU arbitrators and secretaries including technical trainings on arbitration skills using the ILO's Manual for arbitrators. Additional training on labour dispute prevention and resolution was conducted for all DHU mediators and arbitrators together with members of the Tripartite Committee. With the enhanced arbitration skills, arbitrators are able to resolve disputes in compliance with the law. Additionally, with the improved capacity, the Tripartite Committee is able to effectively implement its mandate in complimenting the work of the DHU on dispute prevention and resolution

description.narrative:
By end of 2022, President’s Office – Labour, Economic Affairs and Investment, (PO-LEAI)- Zanzibar and the Prime Minister’s Office – Labour, Employment and Person with Disability (PMOLYED) – Tanzania Mainland had taken measures to strengthen the capacities of its labour officers and inspectors to implement Strategic Compliance Plan, including execution of strategic labour inspections
Court of Appeal Case Digests/Case Management Guide was developed and published in August 2023 for dissemination to strengthen the capacities of Tanzania institutions for dispute prevention and resolution, as it provides reference for the improvement of case management and operational procedures for such institutions From June 2022, with resources available under the UNDP Multi Partner Trust Fund Office (One fund), UNDP funded Improved labour market governance and promotion of tripartism TZA/18/02/OUF and Enhancing implementation of labour standards by ending violence against women and children through a social dialogue framework ; TZA/20/01/OUF, 25 labour inspectors were trained on inspection skills to conduct strategic inspections. The training enhanced capacity of inspectors and, as a result, the POLEAI inspectors were able to develop a Strategic Compliance Plan targeting construction and private security sectors. The Plan is currently being implemented with ILO technical assistance Utilizing one fund reaosurces, ILO's continued its technical assistance that included training workshops and technical support and followups from the ILO relevant experts and units, during the year 2022, the Prime Minister’s Office – Labour, Employmnet and Person with Disability (PMOLYED), is currently implementing a Strategic Compliance Plan (SCP) on labour inspection with a focus on construction and transportation sectors. The SCP was developed with support during the 2021-22 biennium from the ILO and its implementation has enhanced compliance of work places with labour laws. This implementation has facilitated formalization of employment contracts in various sectors, in which, 3,414 workers who were working without contracts have now been entered into formal written Employment contracts
With ILO's technical assistance of the ILO, selected labour cases from Court of Appeal of Tanzania were collected into a Labour Case Digest which was review with a close collaboration with the Tanzania Labour Court for publication and dissemination in August 2023 by the judiciary.

description.narrative: Following a capacity building workshop in November 2022 with 30 high level participants from the tripartite constituents in Zanzibar and Main Tanzania, six collective agreements in Zanzibar were concluded in the hospitality, petroleum and private security industries, and 36 agreements in Mainland Tanzania in the agricultural sector. The ILO provided technical support, policy advice and capacity building to the tripartite constituents in both Mainland Tanzania and Zanzibar throughout the biennium. The National Roadmaps on Collective Bargaining which were adopted in December 2021 provided an integrated platform for action to address the challenges faced in effective bargaining. A capacity building workshop on collective bargaining was conducted in November 2022 with 30 high level participants from the tripartite constituents in Zanzibar and Main Tanzania. In preparation of the workshop, the ITC-ILO training package on industrial relations was adapted to the national context and piloted in both jurisdictions. A study on “Labour Relations in the Civil Service in Tanzania” was developed in consultation with the tripartite constituents and will be validated during the next biennium. The work in Tanzania was carried out with support from the Multi Partner Trust Fund Office, UNDP as well as the UNDP funded project on Improved labour market governance and promotion of tripartism TZA/18/02/OUF.

description.narrative: The Government of Tanzania, following the appointment launch and capacity development of the New Wage Board who conducted the survey in consultation with the social partners and other stakeholders, adopted in November 2022, a new minimum wage which came into effect in January 2023. Social partners in the hotel/tourism sector in Zanzibar signed one collective agreement at the enterprise level on 5 April 2022 which defined intervals for yearly wage increases (clause 6), established allowances (clause 12), including for housing (clause 5) and years of service (clause 7). Another collective agreement at the enterprise level in the hotel/tourism sector level was signed on the 30th June 2022 covering both Mainland Tanzania and Zanzibar which established wage floors (clause 10.1.1), defined wage increases for 2023 and 2024 (clause 10.1.3) and one-off wage increases (clause 10.1.2). The collective agreement also established allowances (clause 10.1.4) including night work allowance (clause 6.1) and bonuses (clause 10.2) such as for years of service (clause 12.1) as well as overtime pay (clause 5.1). From April to June 2022, the ILO, with the support of the UNDP Multi Partner Trust Fund Office, extended technical assistance to build the capacity of all members and the secretariat of the Wage Board for private sector (Mainland Tanzania) on social dialogue and international labour standards for them to effectively implement their mandate. The ILO provided technical support during the period between February 2022 to April 2023 which led to the signing of the collective agreements. That support included: i) producing training manuals on collective bargaining which covered a wage bargaining component, ii) organising and facilitating a tripartite workshop on collective bargaining for 30 representatives of the constituents with a session on wage bargaining. This was carried out under the scope of the Multi Partner Trust Fund and within the framework of the National Roadmap on collective bargaining.
